div.head: VI As 8.2
div.ab: ⁊ gif þonne þæt gebyrige, þæt ænig mægð to þan strang sy and to þam mycel, innon landes oððe uton landes, XIIhynde oððe twyhynde, þæt us ures rihtes wyrnen ⁊ þone þeof foren forstande, þæt we rídan be eallum mannum tó mid þam gerefan þe hit on his mónunge sy.

Et si eueniat, quod aliqua cognatio (tribus) ad hoc magna sit et fortis, in terra uel extra, tƿelfhyndes uel tƿihindes, ut rectum nostrum difforciet ac furem defendat, adeamus omnes una cum preposito, in cuius mannicione est (sit).

⁊ gif þonne þæt gebyrige, þæt ænig mægð to þan strang sy and to þam mycel, innon landes oððe uton landes, XII hynde oððe twyhynde, þæt us ures rihtes wyrnen ⁊ þone þeof foren forstande, þæt we rídan be eallum mannum tó mid þam gerefan þe hit on his mónunge sy.

Und wenn nun der Fall vorkommt, dass eine Sippe so stark und so gross ist — innerhalb [dieser] Landschaft oder ausser Landes, von 1200 [Schilling Wergeld] .oder 200 —, dass sie uns unser Recht verweigern und [sie] für den Dieb schützend eintritt: dass wir in gesammter Mannschaft hinzureiten mit dem [Grafschafts-]vogte, der es [Sheriff] im Bezirke jenes [Diebes] ist,

And if it then happens that a kindred is so strong and so large — within [this] district or outside it, of 1200 [shillings' wergild] or 200 — that they refuse us our right and [it] steps in to protect the thief: that we ride there with all our men, with the [shire-]reeve in whose district that [thief] is,

Again, if it happens that any group of kinsmen — whether nobles or commoners within or beyond the borders of our district— become so strong and powerful as to prevent us from exercising our legal rights, and stand up in defence of a thief, we shall ride out against them in full force with the reeve in whose district the offence takes place.

And if it then happens that any kindred is so strong and so large, within the district or outside it, whether men of a twelve-hundred wergild or of a two-hundred, that they refuse us our rights and stand up for a thief, we are to ride thither with all our men with the reeve in whose district it is.
div.note: Liebermann prints ‘tƿelfhyndes’, ‘tƿihindes’ with the OE letter wynn (ƿ), now kept as printed (October 2026; before, normalised to w). H's ‘wyrnen … forstande’ was emended by Schmid to ‘wyrne … forstanden’. The German sentence continues in 8.3.

Gemeinfreie Sippen können polizeigefährlich mächtig sein auch nach III 6 = IV 3. — Im Q sind die Endungen -es Französische Plurale. — Vgl. Gl Wergeld 4ff.
Kindreds of common freemen can be powerful enough to endanger public order according to III 6 = IV 3 too. — In Q the endings -es are French plurals. — Cf. Gl Wergeld 4ff.

Bessere ‘in dessen Bezirk es vorkommt’ wie II 25, 1. — ‘Gerichtsbann’ Schmid, allein manung hat territoriale Bed. auch sonst (s. Toller); diese ist hier erfordert, da andere Vogteien laut 8, 3 angrenzen. — Dass unter dem Vogt [Q bleibt bei allgemeinem Ausdruck praepositus, selbst 8, 4, wo er doch scyra beibehält, also Grafschaft meint; ebenso ‘reeve’ Price-Thorpe] ein Sheriff (s. d. Gl 9d. e; so Schmid 975b; Pol Mai I 7) gemeint sei, folgt aus 8, 4, wonach die Vogteien notwendig aneinander grenzen, was nur bei Grafschaften zutrifft, nicht z. B. bei königlichen Städten oder den nicht vom Adel abhängigen Gütern

Read rather ‘in whose district it occurs’, as II 25, 1. — ‘judicial ban’ Schmid, but manung has a territorial meaning elsewhere too (see Toller); this meaning is required here, since according to 8, 3 other reeveships adjoin. — That by the reeve [Q keeps to the general expression praepositus, even in 8, 4, where he nonetheless retains scyra and so means shire; likewise ‘reeve’ Price-Thorpe] a sheriff (see that word in Gl 9d. e; so Schmid 975b; Pol Mai I 7) is meant follows from 8, 4, according to which the reeveships necessarily border on one another, which holds only for shires, not, e.g., for royal towns or for estates not dependent on the nobility

Probably the (burghal) district attached to London. No such district is mentioned in the text of the Burghal Hidage which has come down to us. But the burgware of London are frequently mentioned in the Sax. Chron., and the existence of a burghal district is implied in the preamble to this code.
